title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_0RB0RA_1RB1RF_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_0RB0RA_1RB1RF_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of phases: a counter n becomes 8·(n div 3) + d, where the residue of n mod 3 and a word P of blocks to its left decide d and the next word. Lean proves the rounds of a phase for all lengths, and the residue-0 phase end: (L 0 1a+1 0, 3m + 3) → (L 0, a + 8m + 11). No halting transition was found in the word dynamics (trusted, by simulation), so the machine may well run forever, but the word dynamics is unbounded and not understood. Update, 13 November 2026: a search of all tails of at most 26 cells with the generic class map finds halting classes; the nearest needs 107 prescribed residues mod 3 in a row from the start of the run (observed, not proved). The machine is a cryptid.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 79,601 cells have been visited and 52,973 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: The rounds of a phase
claims.text: The start of a phase, one round (three 1s of the counter become four pairs 01), and any number of rounds at once, for every count and every word P, and a whole phase for residue 0: a word ending in a block 0 1^(a+1) 0 and n = 3m + 3 give the word without that block and n = a + 8m + 11.

claims.title: The phase map agrees with the machine
claims.text: At all 8 transitions between the 9 phase starts of the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps (the last at step 65,841,736, n = 17,368) the measured word map predicts the next phase start.

claims.title: No halt in the explored word dynamics
claims.text: Exploring the word dynamics breadth first for every sequence of residues (600 words, the longest 43 cells): no transition halts, and every one returns to a phase start (the same word graph as its relabelled twin).

claims.title: The real orbit
claims.text: From the first phase start (step 17, P empty, n = 6), computed exactly: no halt in 2,000 phases (n then has 2,833 bits); 32 distinct words, the longest 20 cells.

claims.title: Probably nonhalting, for a structural reason not yet proved
claims.text: Unlike Antihydra-type machines, no halting word is known here, so there is no coin-flip argument for a halt. The word behaves like a stack of nested counters (a residue-0 phase absorbs its last block into the counter, the others push or edit blocks), and the explored part of it never halts; a proof would need an invariant on all reachable words.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 0 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m mod 3) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (10 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 6 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 167,895 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 4,187 of the run (A = 0, U = 1, m = 126, B = 0 16): 167,895 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 237,585 bits (about 10143,039 steps of the machine). 115 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 28 cells.

claims.title: No halting class among 5,000 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 5,451 found, to depth 43. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

claims.title: A halting class is reachable, 107 rounds away
claims.text: The same search restricted to contexts of at most 26 cells runs to the end: 3,089 contexts (488 longer ones are reached but not expanded), and 2 of their classes halt. The nearest is 107 rounds from the starting context: after the remainders 22 03 23 0 23 03 23 04 23 03 24 05 24 04 24 03 23 03 23 04 23 03 24 05 24 05 24 04 24 05 (mod 3) the tail is 01011011, and with m ≡ 2 (mod 3) the machine halts before the next event (all six simulated values of m halt). So, granted the class map, a halt is possible, but only through one prescribed sequence of 107 remainders or a longer one; with remainders like fair dice that is one chance in 3107 per try. The orbit computed has not come near it.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Granted the class map (observed, not proved), it halts exactly if the orbit ever reaches a halting class; the nearest known one needs 107 prescribed remainders mod 3 in a row. A Collatz-like question about one orbit: a cryptid.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. A counter grows by a factor of about 8/3 each phase, and its residues mod 3 edit a word of blocks on the tape. A halting word exists, but the nearest one needs 107 particular residues in a row, so no simulation will see it; whether the real sequence ever produces one is the open question.

facts.text: per phase: the rounds of a phase are proved in Lean for every count.
of the word dynamics explored for every residue sequence: no halt.
No halt in the C simulator; 79,601 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Phases: a counter and a word
html: Stop the machine every time the head, in state B, is at the right end of the tape with the tape reading
P 1^n 0 B>0

a word P (ending in 0), a block of n 1s and the fixed end 0. During a phase the head goes back and forth between the counter and the right end: each round takes three 1s from the counter and writes four pairs 01 at the right (Lean, for all counts). When fewer than three 1s are left, the residue n mod 3 decides what happens: the head goes on into P and edits its last blocks, and on the way back the pairs become the next counter. So n becomes 8·(n div 3) + d, where d and the next word depend only on P and n mod 3.

In the words, a residue-0 phase absorbs the last block of P into the counter (proved in Lean for the machines with factor 8/3), while the other residues push new blocks or edit the last ones, often through a smaller phase of the same kind run on a block of P. So P is a stack of nested counters.

sections.heading: Does any word halt?
html: The word map was measured by simulation (each pair of a word and a residue is run from three sample counts, which must agree). Exploring the word dynamics breadth first for every sequence of residues (600 words, the longest 43 cells): no transition halts, and every one returns to a phase start (the same word graph as its relabelled twin).
From the first phase start (step 17, P empty, n = 6), computed exactly: no halt in 2,000 phases (n then has 2,833 bits); 32 distinct words, the longest 20 cells.

So, unlike Antihydra-type machines, there is no known halting word and no probabilistic argument for a halt: the machine is plausibly nonhalting. A proof would need a description of every word the dynamics can reach, closed under all residues, together with the phase ends proved in Lean for each kind of word. That was not done here.

Related machines. 1RB---_0RC0RE_1RD1RF_1LE0LB_1RC0LD_1RC1RA and 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_0RB0RA_1RB1RF_1RD--- are the same table with the states relabelled (no mirror), started in different states: their phase rules, word maps and Lean files are the same up to the name of the phase state (C and B), and only their orbits differ. 1RB---_1RC1RE_1LD0LE_1RF0LC_0RD0RA_0RB1RD has the same kind of phase, with factor 10/3 instead of 8/3.

sections.heading: Some remainder classes halt, 107 rounds away
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 0 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m mod 3) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 6 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 4,187 of the run (A = 0, U = 1, m = 126, B = 0 16): 167,895 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 237,585 bits (about 10143,039 steps of the machine). 115 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 28 cells.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 5,451 found, to depth 43. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

A halt is reachable. The same search restricted to contexts of at most 26 cells runs to the end: 3,089 contexts (488 longer ones are reached but not expanded), and 2 of their classes halt. The nearest is 107 rounds from the starting context: after the remainders 22 03 23 0 23 03 23 04 23 03 24 05 24 04 24 03 23 03 23 04 23 03 24 05 24 05 24 04 24 05 (mod 3) the tail is 01011011, and with m ≡ 2 (mod 3) the machine halts before the next event (all six simulated values of m halt). So, granted the class map, a halt is possible, but only through one prescribed sequence of 107 remainders or a longer one; with remainders like fair dice that is one chance in 3107 per try. The orbit computed has not come near it.
That makes the machine a cryptid: whether it halts is a question about one orbit of a Collatz-like map, and nothing known decides it.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 79,601 cells (13 left of the start, 58,262 right), with a density of 1s of 0.665.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A counter n multiplied by about 8/3 per phase, whose residue mod 3 edits a word P of blocks on the tape; a halting word is reachable, but only through 107 prescribed residues in a row (observed; a cryptid).
